title: Answers to Political Questions: The Pakistani Elections | America's Recognition of Kosovo's Independence | Bush's African Tour
text:
Answers to Political Questions

The Pakistani Elections | America's Recognition of Kosovo's Independence | Bush's African Tour

First: According to the preliminary results of the Pakistani elections published yesterday, after the counting of votes for 222 of the 272 seats of the National Assembly, the People's Party, which Benazir Bhutto used to lead, won 73 seats, the Muslim League (Nawaz Sharif wing) 63, and the Muslim League (Quaid wing), which supports Musharraf, only 29 seats... This is a picture close to the truth of the final results... and it is enough to show the extent of the decline in support for Musharraf. Does this mean that America's influence in Pakistan has declined to the point of receding from Pakistan, in exchange for the return of British influence to Pakistan through Bhutto's party?

To answer this question, the following matters must be mentioned:

1- It was clear that Musharraf had lost his popularity among the Muslims ever since he threw himself into America's arms and supported it in the war on Afghanistan, and made Pakistan's airspace available to it as a launching pad for the aggression against Afghanistan... then the massacres he carried out in the tribal area and the border regions with Afghanistan, and after that the massacre of the Red Mosque that he carried out... and the bloody events that followed, which he carried out in (Swat) and elsewhere...

2- For this reason America saw that Musharraf had to be supported by the secular movements. So it concluded a deal with Britain, and consequently between Musharraf and Benazir Bhutto, who had been (exiled) in Britain for a number of years, during which she had gone along with Britain, and consequently Britain's influence in her party had become strong. The deal stipulated that the charges of corruption... that had been directed at Bhutto would be lifted and she would be returned (clean) to Pakistan, that her party would help in the election of Musharraf as President of the Republic according to the previous parliamentary electoral body, that is, before the current parliamentary elections, and that Bhutto would then become prime minister... that is, a sharing of power: Musharraf President of the Republic and Bhutto head of the government. America was compelled to do that in order to preserve Musharraf's survival in power as a guarantee of its interests, and it accepted to concede something to Britain, that is, to Bhutto, because it feared that it would lose most of its influence, if not all of it, by losing Musharraf, in view of the popular campaign of the Muslims against him in Pakistan.

Matters proceeded according to the deal: Bhutto returned, and Musharraf was elected President of the Republic, as the People's Party in parliament gave up standing against his election... and Bhutto began to tour Pakistan with her well-calculated campaigns.

3- However, Bhutto noticed the extent of the people's hatred for Musharraf, so she exploited this point in the manner of the English and rode the wave, and her campaigns came to be focused not on the limits of the deal but on bringing Musharraf down. She succeeded in that to a degree that worried America and consequently Musharraf... then Bhutto was assassinated... Nevertheless, the party's popularity increased and did not decrease, and the party almost attracted not only its supporters but all of Musharraf's opponents, not out of love for the People's Party but out of hatred for Musharraf.

4- This was an alarm bell for America, and it feared that Bhutto's party would sweep the elections, not only by winning a majority, but that it might reach two thirds, which would make the possibility of uprooting Musharraf, and consequently American influence, and the return of English influence, possible, indeed easy. At that point it decided to allow Nawaz Sharif to return to Pakistan, for his party to take part in the elections and to appear in the guise of an opponent of Musharraf, and thereby to attract a section of Musharraf's opponents, so that the votes of the opponents would not all go to Bhutto's party.

5- Nawaz Sharif is one of America's former agents. America became angry with him when, as prime minister, he was unable to prevent the Pakistani army from supporting the Mujahideen of Kashmir in the occupation of the Kargil heights at the end of the last century (1999 CE), which dealt a crushing blow to the ruling Janata Party in India under the leadership of Vajpayee, who was loyal to America.

America had won Vajpayee's loyalty after exerting every effort in that, because the Congress Party, loyal to the English, had led the rule of India for many years. So when Vajpayee, loyal to America, reached power, America supported him militarily, economically and in security, hoping that its influence would enter and settle in India (or at least that it would share with Britain), after the Congress Party had monopolised the rule of India for several decades.

The occupation of the Kargil heights by the Mujahideen of Kashmir with the help of the Pakistani army was a setback, indeed a catastrophe, for Vajpayee's rule... And so America became angry with Nawaz Sharif; then came Musharraf's coup movement, then the withdrawal of the Pakistani army and the Mujahideen of Kashmir from the Kargil heights.

Nawaz Sharif remained (exiled) from Pakistan for about eight years, and America would not accept his return, as a punishment for him, until there came the growing popularity of Bhutto's party, her breach of the terms of the deal, and consequently the expectation that she would obtain two thirds of the votes, or at least a majority, enabling her to form the government alone and change the rules of the game alone.

At that point it became (pleased) with Nawaz Sharif and returned him to Pakistan in a way that showed him as an opponent of Musharraf in his statements, in harmony with Bhutto, to the extent that they showed him as more of an opponent than Bhutto, as they did not lift the restriction on his personal candidacy, but they supported the candidacy of his party!

6- Then the elections were held in this atmosphere, and Bhutto's party and Nawaz's party shared the votes of the opposition to Musharraf, and the preliminary results showed that Bhutto's party obtained neither two thirds nor a majority; rather, it is compelled to a coalition government!

7- From the above it becomes clear that America's scale is still the weightier one:

a) Musharraf is the President of the Republic, and he had introduced constitutional amendments that gave the president some actual powers at the expense of the powers of the head of the government.

b) Nawaz Sharif's party has influential seats (close to Bhutto's party), and it cannot be excluded from influence, whether Bhutto's party is able to form a coalition government with it, or with the Muslim League wing loyal to Musharraf, or even with independents and other minorities... In all cases Bhutto's party will find itself besieged by effective American forces.

c) Moreover, Bhutto's party is a party "gathering" and not a party "bloc" with fixed, defined principles; therefore its loyalties are easily changed. For example, the party previously went through a fluctuation in loyalty: it was close to America before Bhutto's exile to Britain and her staying those years there, where Britain won her loyalty... Therefore it is a party liable to fluctuation.

8- From the above it becomes clear that America's influence is still in Pakistan. The most that there is, is that Britain has found a not inconsiderable place in Pakistan in which to (poke) its nose, which makes something of a political struggle between America and Britain go on in secret: America's influence over Bhutto's party, or Britain's widening of the place in which it (pokes) its nose in Pakistan...

9- In summary, it cannot be said that America's influence in Pakistan has declined to the point of receding because of the election results, even if the temperature of this influence has abated somewhat.

--------------------

Second: (Kosovo) declared its independence yesterday, and the United States hastened to recognise it. It is known that America was behind this independence. Does this mean that the Bush administration wants, by helping the Muslims of Kosovo, to repair its position with the Muslims in the Middle East after its crimes in Iraq and Afghanistan resulting from its continuing aggression there?

Answer:

1- The United States did not support Kosovo's independence for the sake of Islam and the Muslims; rather, this is not in its consideration at all, neither closely nor remotely.

The matter relates to Serbia. Serbia has formed a thorn in the throat of America, which wants to extend its influence in the Balkans, since America's presence in the Balkans enables it to influence and control the region effectively. The Balkans are the gateway to Russia and Central Asia, and likewise the gateway to what America calls ("New Europe") in the Balkans and Eastern Europe, and this control serves America's interests politically, economically, in security and even militarily.

Serbia was a solid obstacle (or at least a hindrance) to this matter, and therefore America took an interest in weakening Serbia. It was behind the separation of Montenegro from its union with Serbia, it was behind the campaign of the Atlantic Alliance against the Serbian army in Kosovo and in Serbia itself, and it was behind the projects for separating Kosovo...

2- The independence of Kosovo is in practice not of the known type of independence of states. According to an international resolution, it keeps Kosovo under international trusteeship in the name of the United Nations, but it is in actual fact an American trusteeship that controls the president of Kosovo, its prime minister and its entire government...

3- As for what made the matter appear as though it were help for the Muslims and their rescue, it is the atrocity of the savage crimes that the government of Serbia committed against the Muslims of Kosovo. It committed there such massacres as made the Muslims in Kosovo look upon NATO, and especially America, as their helper. This is what appeared in the celebrations: America's flags were raised in the celebrations in a quantity almost equal to the flags of (independent) Kosovo, if America's flags were not more numerous.

In summary, America exerted every effort in the matter of Kosovo to weaken Serbia, which is counted on Russia's side, so that the whole of the Balkans would become one of America's fortresses without obstacles. That was neither in support of the Muslims nor to correct America's position among the Muslims in the Middle East, for America's crimes in the lands of the Muslims are continuously escalating.

Supporting the Muslims and rescuing them from the crimes of the Kuffar, whether the criminals are Americans, British, Jews, Russians, Serbs or Hindus... in Afghanistan, Iraq, Palestine, Chechnya, Kosovo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Kashmir... is not undertaken by the Kuffar, for Kufr is one creed. Rather, support and rescue are undertaken by the sincere Mujahid Muslims under the leadership of their Khaleefah, in the state of the Rightly Guided Khilafah.

It is truly painful that savage crimes are committed in the lands of the Muslims and they do not find a sincere Muslim ruler to support them, to the extent that humiliation has brought them to seek their rescue from the Kuffar!

--------------------

Third: Bush is making a visit to five countries in Africa: Benin, Rwanda, Tanzania and Ghana. Does this mean that America is waging a (hot) political campaign against Europe in Africa through these visits?

Answer: The matter is not so, since the five countries that Bush visited are followers of the United States without European contest. He did not put on the schedule of his visit countries counted on France's or Britain's side. Not only that, he did not put on the schedule of his visits countries contested between America and Europe, such as Chad or Kenya... And since he confined his visits to countries that follow America in a settled following, this means that that visit of his is not a political campaign against Europe, neither hot nor cold.

That is on one hand. On the other hand, the President of the United States of America in an election year has (clipped) wings in terms of the effectiveness of foreign policy; they describe him as a lame duck. That is in the case of a successful president, so how about a president like Bush? He is a (crippled) duck!

The weightier view regarding these visits of Bush is that they are for electoral purposes, to support the Republican Party in the elections, for the Democratic Party's campaign focuses on the failure of the Republican Party's foreign policy. Therefore Bush deliberately visits the countries in which he has (respect), to highlight the (not ugly) face of foreign policy. So he visits five countries in Africa in which America has (support), exactly as he visited occupied Palestine and Abbas's Authority, and the Gulf states... for electoral purposes.

Visits like these are usually not for approving projects or solutions so much as for highlighting the warmth of the reception and the red carpet rolled out for him...

14 Safar al-Khayr 1429 AH
20/02/2008 CE
